findings_qualitative.value: Most molecules trace homogeneous structures more extended than the ~15″ field of view; SO and SiO show clumps of ~5–8″

evidence.quote: SO and SiO show more complex structures with smaller clumps of size ∼5–8 [′′] .

findings_qualitative.value: HCO+ abundance is higher in translucent than diffuse clouds, so HCO+ is a poor H2 tracer there; CCH and CH are good tracers, c-C3H2 is not

evidence.quote: We further find that CCH and CH are good probes of H 2 in translucent clouds, but that c-C 3 H 2 is not.

claims.hypothesis: Line-of-sight clouds fall into distinct categories
claims.experiment: Decomposed c-C3H2 absorption into components and compared column densities, linewidths and PDF widths
claims.result: Category I has lower column density, FWHM 5.4 vs 7.5 km/s, PDF width 0.48 vs 0.56

evidence.quote: Clouds in Category I (3 kpc arm, 4 kpc arm, and some GC clouds) have smaller c-C 3 H 2 column densities, smaller linewidths, and smaller widths of their column density PDFs

claims.hypothesis: Turbulence driving is solenoidal or compressive
claims.experiment: Compared PDF widths and derived b with simulations of Federrath et al.
claims.result: Mean width 0.52 vs 0.46 (solenoidal); b<0.5 for all components

evidence.quote: The average width of the column density PDFs is σ η = 0.52, which is close to the value of 0.46 expected for purely solenoidal forcing.

claims.hypothesis: Clouds are diffuse, translucent or dense
claims.experiment: HCO+ column densities to H2 and Av; Mopra emission with RADEX densities
claims.result: Densities <~1e3–5e3 cm-3 and Av mostly 1–5 mag with variable HCO+ abundance
claims.finding: Most clouds are translucent, including those with COMs

evidence.quote: Most clouds detected along the line of sight to Sgr B2 are translucent on the basis of their HCO + column densities

claims.hypothesis: Clouds have sub-structure at ALMA resolution
claims.result: Most structures extended ≥15″; small structures mostly noise-limited except SO, SiO

evidence.quote: Smaller structures suggested by the two-point auto-correlation functions are in many cases dubious due to sensitivity limitations.

why_this_data.value: EMoCA resolves continuum of Sgr B2(N), allowing spatially resolved absorption

evidence.quote: The angular resolution of this survey is high enough to resolve the continuum emission of Sgr B2(N) (see Fig. 1).

why_this_method.value: Powell minimisation chosen for many free parameters

evidence.quote: A good method to deal with a large number of free parameters is the Powell minimisation method

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two-Gaussian decomposition of PDFs rejected in favour of direct standard deviation

evidence.loc: 4.5 Turbulence in diffuse and translucent clouds
evidence.quote: to avoid being biased by the decomposition of the PDFs into two Gaussians, in the following we measure the width of each PDF by directly calculating its standard deviation

limitations_admitted.value: Field of view limited by background continuum and finite resolution; ACA combination would help

evidence.quote: the limited size of the continuum background emission, which results from the spatial filtering of the interferometer, and the finite angular resolution.

limitations_admitted.value: PDF width likely underestimated due to limited field of view

evidence.quote: Hence, the width of their PDFs is likely underestimated.

referee_caveats_inferred: Kinetic temperature unconstrained, so Mach number and b depend on assumed 20/40/80 K
Overlapping velocity components may bias linewidths and column densities
HCO+ abundance profile is assumed and interpolated, not measured
Local-minimum Powell fits depend on initial guesses of a custom code
